description: Störmer-Verlet integration computes the next position from the current and previous positions without explicitly storing velocities: x(t+dt) = 2*x(t) - x(t-dt) + a(t)*dt^2. This is algebraically equivalent to the velocity Verlet / leapfrog method but eliminates velocity storage. It is second-order, symplectic, and time-reversible — ideal for a minimal gravity simulation.
mathematical_formalization: Position Verlet: x_{n+1} = 2*x_n - x_{n-1} + a_n * dt^2. Velocity recovery: v_n = (x_{n+1} - x_{n-1}) / (2*dt). Error: O(dt^4) per step in position, O(dt^2) globally. Symplecticity: the map (x_{n-1}, x_n) -> (x_n, x_{n+1}) preserves the symplectic 2-form.
analogical_connections: Finite differences: the Verlet formula is literally the central difference approximation of the second derivative, connecting numerical PDE methods with ODE integration
Signal processing: the three-point stencil used in Verlet is identical to a second-order FIR filter
Cloth simulation in games: Verlet integration is the standard method for cloth and soft-body physics, showing how gravity sim techniques transfer to graphics
implementation_hypothesis: Store two position arrays: pos_current and pos_previous. Each step: compute acceleration from gravity, apply Verlet update, swap arrays. For velocity (needed for kinetic energy), use the central difference formula. Total memory: 2 * N * dims floats for positions.
experiment_seed: Implement position-Verlet and velocity-Verlet side by side. Verify they produce identical trajectories (up to floating-point). Measure memory usage and cache performance for N=10^6 particles.
